qs.q:
Banning proms? — Which person…

A=Ashton (sees both sides, alcohol one issue, advises safety/smart decisions, let teens choose)
B=Ben (principal banned prom, met with parents/teachers, agreed it was right, kids survived)
C=Carlie (media hype exaggerated, teens drink every weekend anyway, fashion reflection of culture, keep proms)

2. agrees the prom equals unacceptable behaviour?
3. believes alcohol is not a problem only at proms?
4. thinks proms have little to do with achievement?
5. mentions teenagers' mental health?
6. proposes a new kind of celebration?
7. raises the question of social inequality?
8. thinks the choice should be left to teenagers?

4 — thinks proms have little to do with achievement?

7 — raises the question of social inequality?

qs.q:
Armenia makes chess compulsory in schools

"These contemporary exploits have fostered a recent craze for this mind-training board game."

The Armenians are very much into chess in modern times because…
A chess has always been a national obsession.
B they wish to beat other former Soviet states.
C it is an obligatory part of the primary school curriculum.
D their chess players have been successful.
opts: chess has always been a national obsession.
they wish to beat other former Soviet states.
it is an obligatory part of the primary school curriculum.
their chess players have been successful.

qs.q:
Armenia makes chess compulsory

"The education minister says taking the pastime into the classroom will help nurture a sense of organisation among schoolchildren and will teach them the importance of taking care of their duties."

Why did the Armenians decide to introduce chess in primary school?
A To maintain Armenia's status as one of the strongest chess-playing countries.
B To honour their long chess-playing tradition.
C To develop schoolchildren's awareness of responsibility.
D To make the Armenian school system the best in the world.
opts: To maintain Armenia's status as one of the strongest chess-playing countries.
To honour their long chess-playing tradition.
To develop schoolchildren's awareness of responsibility.
To make the Armenian school system the best in the world.

qs.q:
Armenia makes chess compulsory

"Chess will certainly teach him to think logically and improvise, as those are indispensable qualities in life."

What does David's family expect from their son's chess playing?
A To bring him and his family more money in the future.
B To make him part of the national chess team.
C To enable him to beat the local chess whiz kid.
D To help him make rational choices and be resourceful.
opts: To bring him and his family more money in the future.
To make him part of the national chess team.
To enable him to beat the local chess whiz kid.
To help him make rational choices and be resourceful.

qs.q:
Armenia makes chess compulsory

"'By playing chess in class, the children think they're playing, while they are actually doing some serious thinking all the time.' 'It is a great way to cross over between having a true hard-core curriculum and giving young children the chance to play and have fun.'"

What does the US chess expert think about Armenia's primary school curriculum?
A It is well balanced.
B It is very difficult.
C It has a good campaign.
D It puts focus on children's fun.
opts: It is well balanced.
It is very difficult.
It has a good campaign.
It puts focus on children's fun.

qs.q:
Armenia makes chess compulsory

"There are some objections to outbursts of bad temper when they lose, and sometimes tears."

A drawback of children playing chess at an early age is that it can…
A teach children to hide their emotions.
B lead to children developing an obsessive addiction.
C lead to children behaving poorly when defeated.
D result in children playing like adults.
opts: teach children to hide their emotions.
lead to children developing an obsessive addiction.
lead to children behaving poorly when defeated.
result in children playing like adults.

qs.q:

"A £30 chess program can now beat the world champion."

According to the last paragraph, computers nowadays…

opts: bring joy into chess.
are the best chess players.
help the grandmasters.
are pretty demanding.
